run_context: Commodity endpoints, pulled for the first time. The 1 Aug snapshot's _pull_summary.json contains no commodity endpoint at all - searching it for 'commodit' returns nothing - so these were never requested. Every plan since has asserted that screenshots are the only route to commodity prices; that assertion was inferred from a gap in the REQUEST LIST and was never tested against the API. It is now refuted.
tier_c_statement: TIER C. UEX is community-reported and crowdsourced. UEX states its own tolerance as +/-20% on commodities. Never auto-promoted. Nothing from this snapshot has been promoted to the database.

endpoints_attempted_and_refused.interpretation: Requires an id_terminal parameter. A full history pull is 135+ requests, one per terminal present in commodities_prices_all. Not attempted in this run.

freshness_finding.question_asked: Do prices carry a timestamp or a game_version?
freshness_finding.answer: TIMESTAMP ONLY. No game_version, patch or build field exists on any commodity price row.
freshness_finding.why_this_matters: Coverage and freshness are both good - a majority of price rows were touched within a day, and the newest predates this pull by 8 minutes. But WITHOUT a game_version a price cannot be attributed to a patch. A row 9 days old may straddle a patch boundary and nothing in the data says so. Timestamp freshness is not patch provenance.

unexpected_domains.assessment: Benign. That is the source's own API host, appearing in files this pull wrote itself, not in any downloaded payload. Recorded rather than suppressed.

integrity_scan.not_a_malware_scan: A real AV pass is still required before quarantine release.

retrieval_script.change: Six commodity endpoints added to ENDPOINTS; --only= filter added so a subset can be pulled without re-pulling the other twelve.
retrieval_script.defect_fixed_during_this_run: The script's docstring said the token was 'loaded from .env', but the python-dotenv import was wrapped in a try/except ImportError whose handler was a bare pass. python-dotenv is NOT installed in this interpreter, so that handler fired silently, .env was never read, and the script then reported 'UEX_API_TOKEN is not set. Refusing to run.' The token was present in .env the whole time. This is a silent failure reported as a different and entirely plausible failure: the message named a missing credential, sending a reader to hunt for something that was never missing, while the real cause - a missing library - was swallowed by the bare pass. Fixed by parsing .env directly (removing the dependency rather than adding one, which also avoids installing a package outside the repo per hard rule 6) and by making the failure message state which step failed and whether .env exists.

credential_handling: Token read from .env into the request header only. It was never printed, logged, echoed to a console, or written to any file in this snapshot or manifest.
credential_warning: SEPARATE FROM THIS JOB: this UEX token was exposed in a screenshot and has never been rotated. It should be rotated at UEX regardless of this work order.
